title: Route design from an applicable requirement basis
statement: The Skill procedures Module shall route design from an applicable requirement basis within its accountable boundary so that SR-080 can be satisfied without transferring another owner's decisions or state authority.

what.problem: The SR-080 obligation crosses guidance, governance or publication boundaries; an unowned contribution can make a locally valid step appear sufficient for the whole workflow.
what.desired_outcome: Request the first requirement gate, including review of reuse conclusions, before dependent design relies on the basis.

why.rationale: MOD-012 owns the behavior or state needed for this contribution; separating it preserves one accountable owner while allowing the parent SR to compose several contributors.

stakeholders: Authors, reviewers and project decision owners

conditions: When the selected requirement-first workflow exercises SR-080 or reassesses its affected basis.

contexts: The MOD-012 responsibility boundary and its declared logical Interfaces.

how.approach: Apply the allocated criteria through the constrained Functions and explicit contract inputs/outcomes; preserve actual actor decisions, subject identity and known limitations.

how_much.scope: This allocated contribution to SR-080; other contributors, independent assessment, physical recording implementation and product activation remain distinct.

acceptance_criteria: Request the first requirement gate, including review of reuse conclusions, before dependent design relies on the basis.
Permit accepted requirements with unfinished design to proceed only to the authorized next work; changed requirements require applicability reassessment.
assumptions: The selected project contract, scope and required counterpart contributions are identifiable; absence is reported rather than inferred.
constraints: This draft allocation neither activates replacement runtime contracts nor proves implementation or satisfaction.

sources.basis: Draft integrated design from the accepted requirement-first basis. This defines target responsibility and cooperation, not installed capability, design approval, runtime evidence or SQLite adoption.
